chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-‘Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who embraced Islam during the month of Ramadan, and some days had passed from it. Is it upon them to make up for the days that passed, or is their day the one in which they embraced Islam? He said: There is no making up (qada) upon them, nor is their day the one in which they embraced Islam, unless they embraced Islam before the rising of dawn (Fajr).

key_terms.طُلُوعِ الفَجۡرِ: The rising of dawn, marking the beginning of the fasting day.
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: Making up missed obligatory acts, specifically fasting days.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for someone who embraces Islam during Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that new converts are exempt from making up prior days or fasting the remainder of the conversion day, unless they embraced Islam before dawn (Fajr). This ruling highlights the principle of gradual obligation (Tadarruj) in Sharia, ensuring that the burden of worship is manageable for those newly entering the faith. The distinction based on the time of conversion underscores the importance of intention and the specific timing of the call to prayer in determining legal duties.
